title: CReal.evt_attained_max_decides_sign: an attained maximiser for a linear family decides the sign of an arbitrary real
statement: CReal.evt_attained_max_decides_sign is the Extreme Value Theorem's ADR-0603 row 2, mirroring CReal.ivt_exact_root_decides_sign. Let v be an arbitrary real and consider the family CReal.evtLinear v := fun t => mul t v on [0, 1]. If some c in [0, 1] attains the maximum of this family over [0, 1] (mul t v <= mul c v for every t in [0, 1]), then v <= 0 or 0 <= v -- again analytic LLPO. So an operator that produces an ATTAINING maximiser for every uniformly continuous function on a closed interval -- the classical Extreme Value Theorem's conclusion -- is at least as strong as a principle this kernel's order does not have; the conclusion is UNPROVABLE here, not refuted, since it is consistent with Bishop's constructive mathematics. What this fact does NOT supply, unlike its IVT counterpart: any evidence IN THIS LEDGER that the maximality hypothesis is non-vacuously satisfiable (it plainly is -- c=1 attains it when v>=0, c=0 when v<=0, checked by kernel reduction in creal_tests::evt_linear_endpoint_values_reduce_and_flip_with_the_sign_of_v -- but no evidence entry here cites that check, unlike CReal.ivt_exact_root_decides_sign's dedicated non-vacuity evidence row). And, more importantly: ANY positive constructive substitute for EVT. Unlike IVT, this kernel has no CReal.supOn, no approximate-maximum theorem, and no fact stating one -- creal/supremum.rs's own module documentation says CReal.supOn itself is 'still not landed'. This fact is a refutation of the classical conclusion with nothing constructive standing in its place; it is not evidence that EVT has been given a constructive treatment here.

formal.statement: theorem CReal.evt_attained_max_decides_sign : ((x0 : CReal) -> ((x1 : CReal) -> ((x2 : CReal.le CReal.zero x1) -> ((x3 : CReal.le x1 CReal.one) -> ((x4 : ((x4 : CReal) -> ((x5 : CReal.le CReal.zero x4) -> ((x6 : CReal.le x4 CReal.one) -> CReal.le (CReal.mul x4 x0) (CReal.mul x1 x0))))) -> Or (CReal.le x0 CReal.zero) (CReal.le CReal.zero x0))))))

evidence.supports: CReal.evt_attained_max_decides_sign is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.

notes: docs/formalized-math-2026-08/08-ivt-and-evt-measured-against-mathlib.md audits this row against Mathlib's IsCompact.exists_isMaxOn and concludes the Pareto-dominance claim holds for IVT but not for EVT, precisely because of the gap this note records: EVT has a boundary refutation (this fact) with no ADR-0603 row-1 general constructive form behind it. CReal.evt_linear's own field doc in creal.rs makes the same point: bounded_of_uniformly_continuous (a computed BOUND, no attaining point) is the optimal computable substitute available, not a maximiser.
